title: Blended-Beef Extender for Grinders and Schools
one_liner: Sell a fiber-and-protein extender that stretches ground beef 20-30% and adds fiber, instead of trying to replace beef.
customer: Regional ground-beef grinders, further processors, and school and institutional foodservice distributors.
problem: Retail beef hit a record $9.64/lb with the smallest herd in 75 years, and Mexican feeder cattle are halted. Plant-based meat failed as a replacement, so buyers have no cost-relief tool.
solution: A mushroom, legume and oat fiber-protein blend with a clean label, tested in 70/30 and 80/20 beef blends, sold by the ton with USDA-compliant blended-product labeling and recipe support.
why_now: Record beef prices, screwworm-driven supply risk, and GLP-1 users who want more protein and fiber per bite make a cheaper high-fiber blended patty newly attractive.
revenue_model: Ingredient sales per pound, co-development fees, and multi-year supply agreements with distributors.
non_obvious_insight: Plant-based meat lost as an identity swap but wins as a cost and fiber additive inside real beef, where the buyer never has to change what they say they are selling.
first_30_days: Contract a food-science lab to build three blends, send samples to about 10 regional grinders and two school-food distributors, and start FSIS labeling work.

title: Magnetic Maps for GPS-Denied Drone Navigation
one_liner: A data company that maps low-altitude magnetic anomalies and sells the layers that let cheap drones navigate without GPS.
customer: Drone makers and integrators in Drone Dominance and Navy autonomy programs who need GPS-denied performance, and later defense agencies seeking quantum navigation.
problem: Jamming defeats GPS, and magnetic navigation needs detailed low-altitude field maps. Public datasets are coarse, and hardware teams do not want to become mapping companies. The Navy is asking for quantum navigation and degraded-environment navigation.
solution: Fly survey drones carrying vector magnetometers over test ranges, training areas and border regions, publish tiles through an API, and provide a reference navigation filter that drone makers can integrate. Start with the Gauntlet region and US test ranges.
why_now: Cheap, sensitive magnetometers and onboard compute make magnetic navigation practical for small drones. Fleets of attritable drones can also continuously enrich the map. The Navy calls for quantum and degraded-network navigation (verify map resolution claims).
revenue_model: Per-area annual licences ($20-100K per region), per-tile API access, and custom survey work for programs. Defense SBIR funding for range expansion.
non_obvious_insight: The map, not the sensor, is the moat and it compounds. Every drone that flies with a magnetometer improves the map, so the mapping firm becomes the network owner.
first_30_days: Buy two survey rigs and map one test range and one agricultural area. Publish accuracy results. Offer 3 Gauntlet participants a pilot navigation filter and tile access.

title: Blind Validation Enclaves for Clinical AI
one_liner: Confidential-computing sandboxes where a hospital's private patient data and a vendor's private model meet, and only a signed performance report leaves.
customer: Health-system AI governance committees and health-AI vendors (imaging, ambient scribes, risk models), plus payers and insurers of AI performance guarantees.
problem: Hospitals cannot validate vendor claims on their own patients because PHI cannot leave and vendors will not ship weights. Published metrics rarely transfer to local populations. The Joint Commission and the Coalition for Health AI issued responsible-AI guidance in Sept 2025 and planned voluntary certification, so buyers now need evidence.
solution: A managed enclave (confidential VMs and GPUs) deployed in the hospital's own cloud tenant. The vendor's container runs against local retrospective data. Attestation proves that the evaluation code was unmodified and nothing was exfiltrated. The output is a signed report on subgroup performance, calibration and drift, repeated quarterly as post-deployment monitoring.
why_now: Confidential GPUs became generally available on major clouds in 2025, health systems adopted ambient scribes and imaging AI at scale, and Joint Commission and CHAI guidance created a demand for third-party assurance. The vendor-paid validation model is visibly conflicted.
revenue_model: $25-75k per validation (split between hospital and vendor), $10k per quarter monitoring, and payer or insurer programmes.
non_obvious_insight: Neither party trusts the other with its crown jewel, and the usual referee (the vendor) is conflicted. A machine that both sides can cryptographically verify replaces the trusted third party, so the product is the attestation as much as the test.
first_30_days: Partner with one academic medical centre's informatics team and two imaging or scribe vendors for a single use-case pilot. Use an existing confidential-computing offering rather than building infrastructure.

title: Jobsite Translator That Teaches the Trade
one_liner: Live English-Spanish translation for construction crews that also logs each worker's vocabulary and safety instructions, turning toolbox talks into comprehension-verified training and a path to licensure.
customer: Mid-size specialty contractors (electrical, drywall, framing, roofing, concrete) with mixed-language crews, their safety directors, and union or association training funds.
problem: OSHA expects training delivered in a language and vocabulary workers understand. Language gaps cause incidents and keep capable helpers from advancing to licensed journeyman. Supervisors cannot verify comprehension, and ESL classes do not teach jobsite vocabulary.
solution: A phone and earbud app: real-time two-way translation with trade-specific glossaries, personalized micro-lessons built from each worker's actual jobsite phrases, comprehension checks after toolbox talks with signed training records, and an upskilling track toward licensing-exam vocabulary.
why_now: Consumer earbuds with live translation shipped in late 2025 and LLM translation now handles jargon with supplied glossaries. Labor shortages make retaining and upskilling existing crews more valuable.
revenue_model: $15-25 per worker per month paid by contractors, training-fund reimbursement, and a safety-compliance bundle.
non_obvious_insight: Translation removes the barrier in the moment, but the durable value is converting translated moments into a personalized curriculum and compliance record. The trade workforce is a captive, unserved learning audience, and safety compliance is an existing budget line.
first_30_days: Pilot with 2 contractors that have largely Spanish-speaking crews. Use the app in the weekly toolbox talk, then hand the safety director a comprehension-verification report. Charge $20 per worker and test on noisy sites early.

title: Pooled Radiation Test Data for Commercial Chips
one_liner: A subscription database and beam-time broker so satellite builders stop each paying to test the same commercial chips.
customer: Constellation and smallsat builders using commercial parts, defense new-space suppliers, and chip vendors seeking space design wins.
problem: Proliferated constellations (Golden Dome's reported 600-satellite award, Starlink) run on commercial parts. Radiation-beam slots are scarce with multi-month queues, and results live in silos. Roughly the same popular parts get tested repeatedly.
solution: Pool member orders to buy block beam time at university and national facilities, and test the top parts by lot and date code. Publish a member-contributed database of results and anomalies, and broker custom tests. Members trade their data for access.
why_now: Defense demand for proliferated LEO and a wave of well-funded satellite makers are stressing limited test capacity. Commercial-parts-first design is now standard.
revenue_model: $10-50k per year per member. 10-15% fee on brokered custom tests. Sponsored testing from chip vendors.
non_obvious_insight: In a commercial-parts space industry, test data is the scarce asset, not the parts. The group that pools it becomes the standards-setter.
first_30_days: Contact two beam facilities about block-time pricing. Pre-sell five founding memberships to satellite builders at $10k each. Publish a free first report on one popular microcontroller or memory part to establish credibility.

title: Fire-Season Vaults for Fandom Collectors
one_liner: Red-Flag-Warning-triggered pickup and insured off-site storage for graded cards, comics, sealed games and memorabilia kept in wildfire-zone homes.
customer: Collectors holding $50K-$2M of graded trading cards, comics, sealed games and signed memorabilia in wildfire-zone ZIPs or on last-resort plans such as the California FAIR Plan (696,562 policies in June 2026).
problem: A closet of graded cards can be worth more than the contents limit on a distressed-market homeowners policy. Collectibles are usually capped or need scheduling, which retreating carriers avoid. Evacuations give minutes. Vaults exist, but storage is a one-time decision with no urgency trigger, and nobody sells 'fire season' as a product.
solution: Three steps. (1) Photograph and catalog the collection with a card-scanning app and a live price feed, producing a claim-ready inventory. (2) From June to November, the top slice of value moves to a bonded vault under agreed-value cover from a specialty coverholder. (3) The remainder goes in a pre-tagged go-case, and on a Red Flag Warning or evacuation warning within N miles a bonded courier collects it within 4 hours, or the owner drops it at a partner card shop. Everything is returned in December.
why_now: The trading-card boom (Pokemon at 85B+ cards, a $28M Kickstarter TCG, blind-box resale above RMB 1,000 with VCs funding the resale layer) has turned closets into six-figure assets. FAIR Plan exposure hit $768B (secondary source) with a 29.1% rate hike. New carriers expanding under California's Sustainable Insurance Strategy have said nothing about scheduled personal property.
revenue_model: Annual fee of about 0.6-1.2% of stored declared value (storage plus insurance), a $150-400 courier trigger fee per activation, and commission on the agreed-value policy. An average $250K customer is worth about $2.5K a year.
non_obvious_insight: Insurers are retreating from the house, not from the objects. Fandom wealth is small, portable and already authenticated (slab cert numbers), so it is the one wildfire-zone asset you can move in a single trip and value without an adjuster. The business is logistics plus underwriting data, not a vault.
first_30_days: Pre-sell 30 founding memberships through Discord, Reddit and 10 card and comic shops in fire-prone ZIPs (Altadena, Topanga, Santa Rosa, Boulder foothills). Partner with an existing vault and a Lloyd's coverholder rather than building either. Run the first live drill when Santa Ana wind season starts in October-November.

title: Group-Block Attrition and Force Majeure Claims Desk
one_liner: A 48-hour, outcome-priced desk that tells meeting and wedding planners whether the 2026 shocks let them escape or shrink hotel attrition penalties, and files the notices on time.
customer: Association and corporate meeting planners without in-house counsel (100-1,000 attendees), destination-wedding planners, DMCs, and youth-sports or choir tour operators holding hotel room blocks.
problem: Hormuz closure (2 Mar 2026), jet-fuel-driven capacity cuts and fare hikes, and UAE hospitality disruption mean groups cannot fill contracted blocks, while booking lead times shrank from 37.5 to 33 days. Attrition clauses often penalize around 20% shortfalls, and force-majeure wording and notice deadlines, not the law, decide outcomes. Small planners miss the 7-30 day notice windows and pay in full.
solution: Upload the contract for a clause map covering the attrition table, cure and mitigation duties, force-majeure triggers, and deadlines. The desk generates the notice letters, sends deadline alerts, and provides a negotiation script and a walk-away vs renegotiate calculator. A partner hospitality lawyer handles escalations at a fixed fee. Cases where the hotel resold freed rooms at higher rates argue mitigation, not force majeure.
why_now: The 2026 disruption produced a wave of disputes between now and winter events. Europe summer ADR rose 4-6% and Turkey flights rose 25% as trips rerouted. In those markets hotels can resell freed blocks at higher prices, which weakens their damages claims.
revenue_model: $390 flat for the clause map and deadline pack, about 15% of penalties avoided as a success fee, and fixed-fee lawyer escalations. An annual $1,200 deadline-tracker subscription is aimed at DMCs.
non_obvious_insight: The strongest argument is often mitigation, not force majeure. In rerouting hot spots the hotel resells rooms at higher rates and cannot claim losses it did not suffer. The moat is a dataset of clause wording and outcomes, plus never missing a deadline.
first_30_days: Recruit 20 planners from association-executive and wedding-planner forums with a free 'contract triage' of one block. Have one hospitality lawyer review the template letters. Convert the first 5 to paid flat-fee packs and log every outcome to build the clause database.

title: Exoskeleton Hike Rentals for Active Older Adults
one_liner: Trailhead rental hubs and guided exo-hikes that let 60-80 year-olds keep climbing with powered hip assist.
customer: Active adults 55+ (pay $70-120 per day), outdoor retailers and outfitters, senior-living activity directors and trail-gateway towns.
problem: Consumer exoskeletons now exist ($900-2,300, with the leader's models at about $2,000-2,300) but buyers hesitate to spend that on something they have never tried, and older hikers quietly stop hiking as knees and hips fade.
solution: A rental fleet with fitting, safety briefing and waivers, guided group hikes, retailer rental corners, and monthly exo-walks for senior living communities. Renters get a credit toward purchase and we earn affiliate commissions.
why_now: Consumer hip-assist exoskeletons reached the $900-2,300 range with heavy marketing, the leading brand is pushing an 'offline' era with retail and rental hubs, and the active-older-adult demographic is driving the category.
revenue_model: $79 per day rentals, $30 per person guided add-ons, 8-12 percent affiliate on purchases, retail rental-program fees and $1-2k per month senior-living contracts.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is trial, not price, and manufacturers lack local operators; a small team can own the try-before-you-buy channel. The real work is waivers, fitting and injury protocols, which are also the moat.
first_30_days: Buy or borrow four units (about $8k), set up demo weekends at one or two outdoor shops or campgrounds near a popular trail, run a senior-center exo-walk, and start charging rentals from week two.

title: Benefits Administrator for Pet-Care Subsidies
one_liner: When hundreds of millions in philanthropy and city funds must reach the right households through thousands of small clinics, someone needs the HSA-administrator equivalent: eligibility, vouchers, payment and audit.
customer: Foundation grantees and programs (Duffield and PetSmart Charities recipients), county animal services and spay-neuter voucher programs. Clinics are the redemption side.
problem: Duffield committed $250M over 5 years, starting with 250 grants of $10K plus $10M in multi-year awards. Grantees run eligibility by paper forms and spreadsheets, clinics wait weeks for reimbursement, funders cannot compare cost per pet outcome, and fraud and overhead eat funds.
solution: Verify proxy eligibility (SNAP, Medicaid, housing-voucher documents or benefit APIs), issue capped QR or card vouchers by procedure category, pay clinics within 5 business days, and export standardized reporting (pets treated, cost, outcome, declined) to funders. Define a shared outcome taxonomy that becomes the field standard.
why_now: The $250M Duffield commitment (2026-09-17) and PetSmart Charities' $100M created hundreds of new grantees at once. Card-issuing and instant-payout APIs let a small team run a closed-loop voucher program.
revenue_model: 4-7% administration fee on disbursed dollars (funded from grant overhead lines), SaaS fee per grantee, and data and reporting subscriptions for funders.
non_obvious_insight: Money is not the binding constraint; distribution rails are. Human benefit administrators (HSA and EBT processors) became large businesses because funders needed accountability. About 250 first-round grantees have no back office, so the standard-setter for outcomes measurement owns the funders' reporting.
first_30_days: Contact 20 first-round grantees and 5 county animal services. Offer a free voucher tool to one program with a $10K grant, run through 3 clinics, and publish an outcomes one-pager. Then brief funder program officers on standardized reporting.

title: Closing-Risk Radar for New-Construction Loan Officers
one_liner: Forecasts which locked new-build closings will miss their rate-lock window, using permit and inspection data plus builder history, so loan officers extend cheaply or re-price before the buyer walks.
customer: New-construction loan officers and mortgage teams (builder-preferred lenders, community banks), title companies, and small builders' sales managers.
problem: 80-90% of new-home sales need rate buydowns, and completions fell 27.1% as crews vanish, foundations sit idle and electricians are delayed up to 2 months. Closing dates slip, locks expire and buydown funding is stranded. A West Virginia builder is at risk of losing about 40 closings. Nobody forecasts construction slippage, only rates.
solution: For each locked loan, ingest the address and pull permit and inspection status from municipal portals, add the builder's stage photos or one-question SMS replies, and output a slip probability and the cheapest date to extend. Add a monthly builder reliability scorecard for lender risk and builder-relations teams.
why_now: Buydown-dependent sales, mortgage rates near 7%, falling completions and forecast 2027 starts down 2-4% mean lock-expiry losses will climb. LLM-based extraction from messy municipal portals is now cheap.
revenue_model: $25-50 per monitored loan or $400-800 per month per loan officer. Enterprise scorecards for lender risk teams.
non_obvious_insight: Loan officers care about the construction calendar as much as the rate curve, and they have direct fee income at stake when a lock lapses, unlike builders who learn late. Public inspection sequence is a surprisingly strong predictor of slip, and the reliability scorecard is a byproduct with its own buyer.
first_30_days: Sell to five new-construction loan officers in Texas and the Southeast. Each shares 20-40 pending closings. Build the forecast manually in spreadsheets from portals and show five saves in 30 days.

title: Compliance Rail for Verified Bio-AI Labs
one_liner: A 'SOC 2 for AI-directed biology': fast dossiers plus continuous evidence collection that let small labs qualify for, and keep, verified access to frontier bio-AI.
customer: Small biotechs, CROs, academic cores and AI-bio startups applying to verification programs (Anthropic expects hundreds of organizations in week one); later insurers and pharma partners that request attestations.
problem: Trend chain: frontier providers now gate relaxed bio safeguards behind credential, security and ethics-oversight review. Next, each provider and government runs a slightly different program. Then small labs discover they lack security staff, an oversight committee, or records separating AI proposal, human edit and robot execution (a gap Lab Manager flags, since CDC and WHO frameworks predate autonomous systems). Each application becomes bespoke paperwork.
solution: Week 1: a 5-day 'verification-ready' dossier covering security-control mapping (SOC 2 and ISO 27001-lite), personnel credential packet, data-retention and access configuration, and a dual-use risk register. Optionally add a rent-an-oversight-committee: an independent biosafety and dual-use review board with documented minutes. Month 3 onward: connectors to ELN, LIMS, robot logs and AI-provider logs produce an audit trail and a portable attestation that is reused across providers.
why_now: Anthropic's Life Sciences Verification Program launched Sept 17, 2026, with 30-day data retention and 'hundreds of organizations' expected in the first week. Other providers are likely to follow (an inference). Autonomous labs are multiplying with no accountability standard.
revenue_model: $3-8k per dossier, $1.5-4k/month for oversight-committee and evidence subscription, and per-attestation fees from providers or insurers.
non_obvious_insight: Relaxed safeguards become a competitive credential the way SOC 2 became table stakes in SaaS. The bottleneck is not the AI provider's review but small organizations' inability to package proof. Once two or more providers run programs, a portable attestation beats bespoke applications, and the evidence stream also feeds insurers.
first_30_days: Turn the public criteria into a 40-point readiness checklist. Sell a $1.5k readiness review to 20 startups via SynBioBeta and LinkedIn. Partner with an IBC or biosafety consultancy for the oversight-committee product. Ship the dossier template.

title: Cash Advances Against Steam Payouts
one_liner: A receivables-and-ad-float lender for live Steam games, underwritten from the studio's own Steamworks wishlist and sales data instead of the game's quality.
customer: Steam-live indie studios and micro-publishers with roughly $50k-$1M a year in net Steam revenue and 100+ reviews. They pay a flat fee of about 8-12% on each advance, repaid from Steam payouts.
problem: Valve pays about 30 days after month-end, so a launch-week spike reaches the bank up to two months later. In that gap the studio sees ads producing wishlists at a profit (say $1-2 per wishlist, with 15-25% converting to first-week sales) but has no cash to scale the spend, pay for a console port or fund localization. Indie Fund and new funds like Blue Ocean's $30M (2026) back development, not post-launch receivables. Banks treat games as hit-driven lotteries.
solution: A 'Payout Bridge'. The studio connects a read-only Steamworks financial and wishlist key. We forecast net receipts for the next 60-90 days from launch-day wishlists, demo conversion, regional mix and refund rate. We advance 30-50% of that forecast, or pay ad platforms and streamers directly as an 'ad float'. The studio points its Steam payout to a sweep account so repayment comes off the top. A free 'Steam funnel benchmark' dashboard built on the same keys is the top of the funnel and the data moat.
why_now: Steam gets roughly 20k releases a year, so marketing spend, not development, is now the main cost and the main cash-flow gap. Small funds are proving capital appetite for indies in 2026. Steam Machine (June 2026) and Steam Frame (Sept 2026) are widening the PC base. LLM tooling makes per-game underwriting cheap enough for $10-40k tickets.
revenue_model: A flat 8-12% fee on each advance, 60-120 day terms, with a fee premium for the ad-float product. Later: a subscription for the benchmark dashboard, and a securitized pool sold to a credit fund.
non_obvious_insight: A lender doesn't need the right tail that VCs obsess over. The first 30 days of Steam sales track launch-day wishlists within a fairly tight band, and Valve is a reliable payer. So credit risk is behavioural (the studio changing its bank details) and can be solved with a sweep account, not with taste in games. Underwrite the wishlist funnel and ignore game quality.
first_30_days: Ship the free Steamworks-key benchmark dashboard and seed it in Steam dev Discords, r/gamedev and the wishlist-marketing newsletters. Raise a $150-250k first-loss pool from angels or a small credit line. Manually underwrite 5-10 advances of $10-40k for studios that just launched or have a Next Fest spike. Get a fintech lawyer to structure it as a purchase of receivables.

title: Texas Data-Center Water Filing and Attestation
one_liner: A fixed-fee compliance service that meters, calculates, files and PE-attests data-center water reports for the operators who ignored Texas's mandatory water survey.
customer: About 280 non-responding Texas data centers (colos, crypto miners, enterprise sites, edge facilities) and developers of the roughly 1,800 projects held in the ERCOT queue. The operator or developer pays.
problem: Only 17% of 341 surveyed Texas data centers answered the mandatory 2025 water survey (maximum fine $500). On Aug 3 the governor froze ERCOT connection approvals pending a water and energy audit, and TWDB owes an update by Oct 14, 2026. Non-reporting is about to become a crime and a bar to TCEQ permits and interconnection. Small operators have no in-house water or regulatory staff.
solution: A turnkey filing: interpret the survey, verify or install non-invasive clamp-on flow metering on make-up and blowdown lines, reconcile utility bills, compute WUE plus scarcity-adjusted and grid-indirect water, then have a Texas licensed PE sign an attestation. Keep an audit-ready data room and issue quarterly updates as rules change.
why_now: The freeze, the Oct 14 update and the coming criminal penalties all land within weeks. A stamp from an independent PE unblocks permits and interconnection, and nobody else sells it to the long tail.
revenue_model: $5-15k per-facility filing package, $2-5k/month recurring attestation, $50-200k portfolio deals. Anonymized data becomes the first scarcity-adjusted benchmark set.
non_obvious_insight: The hyperscalers will self-certify. The 83% who did not respond, mostly small and mid-size operators, will be the first enforcement targets. Enforcement demand arrives suddenly, and whoever has met 50 operators and installed 50 meters in the first wave owns the reference dataset.
first_30_days: Build a list of Texas data centers from public survey and ERCOT queue records. Partner with a Texas engineering firm for PE stamps. Host a 'what to do before Oct 14' webinar, cold-email 100 non-responders, and close the first five filings at $5-10k.

title: Regulatory Slip Desk for Compliance Budget Decisions
one_liner: A probability-weighted deadline desk that tells compliance heads which rules will probably slip, which will not, and which controls are worth building now regardless.
customer: GCs, heads of compliance and CFOs at companies with $200M-$20B revenue facing many regimes at once (EU AI Act, CBAM, CRA, CSRD, US state privacy and AI laws). Secondary buyers are compliance-software vendors timing their sales and investors betting on delay.
problem: Deadlines have become unreliable. AI Act high-risk duties moved to 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III) and 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I) per the tracker (the Omnibus status is unverified), CSRD waves 2 and 3 slipped to 2028, while CBAM and CRA reporting did not move. Teams either overspend on rules that later slip or get blindsided by rules that hold. Law-firm alerts explain what a rule says, not whether it will arrive on time.
solution: A subscription tracker of about 100 obligations, each with the hard date, a written probability of further slip or scope cut with reasons (trilogue calendar, standards readiness, member-state transposition, litigation), and a split between 'no-regret controls' that satisfy several regimes (inventories, logging, supplier data) and 'wait for clarity' items. Trigger alerts ('if standard X is not cited by date Y, slip probability rises'). A public scored track record of every past forecast, plus a quarterly board memo.
why_now: 2025-26 was the year of delays and unwinds: the Digital Omnibus reshuffled AI Act dates, CSRD got stop-the-clock, and several US rules were dropped or vacated (background, verify). Buyers have now been burned in both directions.
revenue_model: $12-40k/year per enterprise seat pack, a $3k/year SME tier sold via newsletter, and a data feed to compliance-software vendors at $30-100k.
non_obvious_insight: Compliance is an options problem, not a deadline problem. Insiders sell obligations as fixed; the value is pricing probability and timing and finding multi-regime no-regret work. A public forecast track record is a moat law firms will not build because they cannot afford to be visibly wrong.
first_30_days: Publish a free 'Slip Index' showing the base rate of deadline moves across the 30 largest EU and US digital rules since 2023. Build a 500-person newsletter via IAPP-style and LinkedIn communities, and pre-sell 10 annual subscriptions at a $6k founder price with a money-back guarantee. Make every forecast in writing with a date.

title: Status-Cliff Benefit Sold Through PEOs
one_liner: A confidential, employer-paid benefit that screens temporary-status workers for alternate immigration relief, tracks work-authorization cliffs, and pre-arranges counsel and family plans before a raid, TPS termination or EAD lapse hits.
customer: Payroll, PEO and staffing firms serving labor-intensive employers (home health, poultry and meat processing, hospitality, warehousing, construction, agriculture), plus the employers themselves. They pay $4-9 per employee per month or $60-120 per screened worker.
problem: Employers with workers on TPS, humanitarian parole, pending asylum EADs or DACA are losing headcount unpredictably. Terminations of TPS and parole programs hit hundreds of thousands of workers with little warning, and automatic EAD extensions ended for renewals filed after late October 2025, so employees now fall out of I-9 validity while renewals are pending. Worksite enforcement and I-9 Notices of Inspection (3 business days to respond) are rising. HR treats it as a compliance chore, then loses 10-30% of a shift overnight.
solution: A benefit package in four parts. (1) A dashboard that projects the work-authorization cliff by employee category and date, with I-9 reverification scripts that avoid discriminatory over-documentation. (2) Confidential relief screening done by a licensed partner attorney for each willing employee (family petitions, pending asylum, U/T visas, SIJS, cancellation, adjustment eligibility) with the employee, not the employer, as the client. (3) An emergency file for each participating worker: signed G-28 on file, memorized A-number card, standby guardianship documents for children, and a hotline for the first 72 hours after a detention. (4) An I-9 pre-audit and a 72-hour Notice of Inspection response playbook.
why_now: TPS and parole terminations, the end of EAD automatic extensions, expanded enforcement, and increased I-9 audits all converged in late 2025 through 2026. Employers can no longer treat immigration compliance as an annual checkbox, and existing I-9 software only tracks expiry dates. It offers no relief screening, no emergency response, and no employee-side counsel.
revenue_model: Per-employee-per-month benefit fee split between the platform and partner law firms (structured as payment to the firm for services rendered, with the third-party-payor consent required by the professional conduct rules), plus per-screening fees and a premium I-9 audit-defense add-on. PEOs and payroll firms get a distribution margin.
non_obvious_insight: The employer's real loss is churn, not fines. In screenings, a surprisingly large share of workers, often a quarter or more in my experience, have a path they never knew about, because no one ever asked in a confidential setting. A worker who is told they have a path stays loyal to the employer that offered it. The right buyer is the PEO's benefits desk, since PEOs already sell legal-plan and EAP riders through one procurement decision.
first_30_days: Pick one vertical (home health agencies, where TPS and parole terminations are hitting staffing hardest) and one state. Partner with 2 immigration firms that have screening capacity. Pitch 3 regional agencies and 1 PEO with a 60-day pilot: 100 employees screened for $6,000, delivered as a de-identified summary of how many have alternate paths. Use the pilot data (headcount saved, cases opened) as the sales deck for the PEO channel.

title: App-Diet Service for the Phone-Upgrade Freeze
one_liner: As phones get unaffordable, today's handset becomes a five-year handset, so old-device performance decides who keeps users.
customer: Banks, wallets, telcos and government digital services with large user bases on 2-3GB RAM Android phones in Africa, India and LatAm.
problem: Memory-driven price rises are stretching replacement cycles. Bloated apps crash on old devices, and churn from that is invisible in analytics.
solution: A fixed-price audit on a real farm of used 2GB phones on 2G/3G. Deliver sub-10MB lite builds and WhatsApp or USSD fallbacks, then a monthly regression retainer. The wedge is a four-week audit for one mid-tier bank or wallet.
why_now: Memory is 30-40% of phone cost, LatAm shipments fell 10%, and GSMA's $40 phone pilot shows the price problem.
revenue_model: $15-40k per audit and $5-10k per month for device-lab monitoring.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone forecasts the next phone. The second-order effect is that the current phone lasts far longer, so performance on old hardware, not features, drives retention.
first_30_days: Buy 15 used phones and publish a teardown of the top 10 fintech apps in Nigeria or India. Use it to book audits.

title: Shared-Aide Pods for 55+ Apartment Buildings
one_liner: One on-site aide team serves 6-10 residents in the same building, delivering assisted-living-style help at a fraction of 1:1 home-care cost.
customer: Owners and operators of independent-living and 55+ apartment buildings (market-rate, senior LIHTC and HUD-202 properties). The payers are middle-income residents and their families, who can't afford $75-130k a year and are stuck on waitlists.
problem: Home care is sold as one aide per client per hour ($35 an hour, about $80k a year for 44 hours a week) only because of legacy billing. Assisted living is at 90% occupancy with almost no new supply before 2030. Residents who age past independent living either move out or go without.
solution: A licensed home-care agency subsidiary (or partnership with one) posts 2-3 aides per shift inside the building. They run scheduled 15-45 minute ADL, medication-reminder, meal-setup and toileting visits, plus overnight response. Dispatch software handles acuity tiers and in-building routing (floors, elevators). Residents buy monthly tiers of about $1,800-3,500, and the property gets a retention amenity.
why_now: NIC MAP shows 57 of 99 metros above 90% occupancy, units under construction at a 2012 low, and no meaningful new supply before 2030. Medicaid HCBS is walled off by 15-month waitlists and labor is scarcer after the 2026 visa pause, so stretching each aide across more clients is the only lever left.
revenue_model: Monthly resident subscription by care tier, with a revenue share or amenity fee to the property owner. Later, Medicaid HCBS or managed-care billing for pods in affordable senior buildings.
non_obvious_insight: Aide hours are cheap to make dense (no drive time, no client-hour minimums) but are priced as if they were mobile. The gap between 1:1 pricing and 1:8 cost is the whole business, and only a property-anchored operator can capture it. Assisted-living-without-the-license is a real category nobody has scaled.
first_30_days: Sign a 90-day pilot with one 100-200 unit 55+ property in a tight market. Subcontract to an existing licensed agency to move quickly, staff a two-aide pod, and target 15 residents at about $2,200 a month. Track aide minutes per resident and move-out avoidance.

title: Independent Pharmacy GLP-1 Aftercare Studios
one_liner: A turnkey cash-pay aftercare membership that gives independent pharmacies their first PBM-free service line.
customer: Independent community pharmacies (~17k in the US). One report has ~41% not dispensing obesity GLP-1s in Q4 2025 over poor reimbursement.
problem: Insiders assume Walmart, CVS and Amazon win GLP-1 care because of scale. Independents get squeezed by PBM reimbursement below cost and skip the category, even though they see patients monthly and pharmacists can check dose, side effects and nutrition.
solution: A 'studio' kit: leased body-composition scale, a protocol (dose-step check, protein and strength plan, red-flag triage), scheduling and billing for a $39-59/month cash membership, and links to pill and vial cash-pay fulfillment. Includes collaborative-practice documents and, where state law allows pharmacist prescribing, protocols for it. Monthly outcomes report to the pharmacist and to referral partners.
why_now: $149-$299 cash pills remove the need for dispensing margin to justify the category. Lilly and Novo cash channels route through retail pharmacies. Big chains launched their own pharmacist support programs in 2026, so independents need a counter-offer.
revenue_model: $199-399/month SaaS per pharmacy plus 20% of membership revenue, plus device lease.
non_obvious_insight: GLP-1 is the first drug category where a pharmacy can earn from services with zero PBM exposure. Independent pharmacists are more trusted locally than a chain's app and have a natural monthly touchpoint.
first_30_days: Partner with one state pharmacy association or wholesaler buying group. Pilot in 5 pharmacies at $49/month. Track retention and a muscle proxy (grip and chair-stand) for the first cohort.

title: Physical-Properties Index for Every SKU
one_liner: A shared 'Gracenote for grasping': weight, center of mass, deformability, best grip points and packaging traits for millions of SKUs, sold to pick-robot makers and brands.
customer: Pick-and-pack robot vendors, 3PLs running robotic induction, CPG and retail brands (for robot-ready packaging certification), and humanoid developers.
problem: Picking robots fail on the long tail because they meet every SKU cold, and brands change packaging without notice. Amazon knows internally, but everyone else relearns per site.
solution: Fill the index from two sources: a scanning rig at partner 3PLs (3D scan, mass, center of mass, slip tests) and give-to-get contributions from robot fleets reporting grasp outcomes. Serve it by GTIN through an API with recommended grasp points and packing advice, and offer brands a 'Robot-Ready' grade that 3PLs reward with lower handling fees.
why_now: Robotic picking is now at scale (Amazon 1M+ robots, Symbotic $2.25B revenue, Maven-style mixed palletizing), and foundation models can use priors like these. A market of data buyers already exists.
revenue_model: API fees per lookup or per robot per month, $2-10k per SKU family for brand certification, and dataset licensing to model labs.
non_obvious_insight: Robots will not scale on smarter grasping alone. The world's goods need a machine-readable physical spec, and brands have a direct incentive because 3PLs and retailers will reward robot-ready packaging. A neutral index can become a standard the way GS1 barcodes did.
first_30_days: Build a $15k scanning rig at a friendly 3PL and scan the top 3,000 SKUs. Release a free tier, sign 2 pick-robot vendors as beta partners, and run one paid brand packaging audit.

title: Blue UAS Bill-of-Materials Origin Auditor
one_liner: Part-by-part origin verification so 60,000-drone orders do not fail on hidden Chinese-origin motors, radios and cameras.
customer: Drone makers and their integrators selling to DoD and public safety, and the primes that must certify their subcontractors' parts.
problem: Compliance requires proving that components meet domestic-content and ownership rules, but sub-tier motors, ESCs, batteries and cameras often trace to opaque distributors. Manufacturers self-certify with spreadsheets and hope a re-labelled part is not found mid-contract.
solution: Upload a BOM and receive origin confidence per part. Cross-check import records, distributor invoices, factory databases and optional lab teardown or spectrum fingerprinting of sample units. Deliver an auditor-ready dossier and alerts when a supplier changes source.
why_now: Drone Dominance orders make component provenance a gating item for tens of thousands of units. About 48 defense firms are IPO candidates and want clean compliance records. Gauntlet winners must scale quickly and can't afford a failed audit (verify statutory citations).
revenue_model: $5-25K per BOM audit, $2-8K per month for monitoring, and per-sample teardown fees.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is not certification but suppliers' unofficial data. Trade-data analytics plus teardown labs beat legal-only compliance firms because they can catch a repackaged part.
first_30_days: Audit 3 drone BOMs for free to build a dataset. Hire a customs-data analyst and a contract RF engineer. Pitch Gauntlet participants directly.

title: Fresh-Fall Meteorite Alerts and Landowner Desk
one_liner: Turn satellite lightning-sensor fireball detections into strewn-field maps within an hour, then broker signed landowner access and sale terms for hunters and dealers who pay for a 24-hour head start.
customer: Serious meteorite hunters, dealers and collectors (a few thousand worldwide), with museums and labs as secondary buyers of fresh, uncontaminated samples.
problem: Value depends on freshness and documentation. A witnessed fall recovered before rain sells for many times the price per gram of desert finds, and in my recollection a Martian meteorite sold for about $5.3M at auction in 2025. Hunters race using scattered social posts and public bolide feeds that arrive late. Landowners own the meteorites in the US, so the hunter who lands the landowner's yes wins.
solution: A pipeline that ingests public geostationary lightning-mapper fireball detections, weather-radar falling-debris signatures and upper-air winds to publish a dark-flight strewn ellipse in minutes. It overlays parcel data and gives the desk a landowner script, a one-page finder-landowner split contract, and a provenance dossier (time, coordinates, radar and satellite evidence) that raises sale price. Paid subscribers get the alert first.
why_now: GOES-19 became the operational eastern US geostationary satellite in 2025, with lightning imagers now covering the Americas and, as I understand it, Europe and East Asia. Open radar data is on the cloud, and the collectibles market is at extremes (a $16.5M single card in Feb 2026). LLM pipelines make a two-person alerting desk feasible.
revenue_model: $15 per month for hunter alerts, a $49 event pass for high-value falls, and 10% of sale value on brokered recoveries. Dealers pay about $300 per month for a priority feed and the landowner contract kit.
non_obvious_insight: Detection is free public data. The scarce input is speed to a signed landowner agreement before rain and rivals arrive. The business is a contracts-and-logistics desk that happens to run on satellite data, and the provenance dossier is the price multiplier.
first_30_days: Script the public fireball feeds and backtest on 2021-2025 falls. Open a Discord with 200 hunters and 5 dealers, and pre-sell 30 annual passes at $99. Offer to run the next credible fall end to end using the contract template, taking a percentage only if material is recovered.

title: Turn Podcast Fans Into Local Chapters
one_liner: A chapter-in-a-box that lets mid-size creators convert engaged, lonely audiences into weekly local meetups, with insurance, host training and venues handled.
customer: Superfans aged 18-34 paying about $12 a month for a local chapter. Creators with 50k-1M followers are the distribution partners on a revenue share. Brand sponsors pay for chapter access.
problem: Insiders treat parasocial attachment as a symptom of loneliness. But an audience with a shared in-group reference is already a pre-formed community, and creators' inboxes are full of 'is there a meetup in my city?' Creators cannot run 40 city chapters themselves because of liability, hosting, venues and safety. Discord and online-only communities do not fix in-person isolation.
solution: The platform reads audience data to find the top 10 fan-dense cities per creator. It recruits and trains volunteer hosts from top fans, provides liability insurance, a code of conduct and venue partnerships (breweries, cafes), and delivers a monthly 'creator drop' built for group listening or viewing. Each chapter runs weekly or biweekly with a 30-40 member target.
why_now: Fan-led IRL groups (run clubs, book clubs, hobby meetups) exploded through 2024-25. Feed fatigue and AI-slop backlash push young adults toward real-world belonging. Creators need revenue beyond volatile ad and sponsor income, and Meetup's post-acquisition policy troubles have left organizers looking for alternatives.
revenue_model: 20-25% of chapter dues, venue referral fees and sponsor packages. A 40-member chapter at $12 a month is $480 a month. Creators keep about 40% of dues.
non_obvious_insight: Parasocial is not the disease, it is the on-ramp. The cheapest cold start for local community is an audience that already shares references. What is missing is boring, outsourceable logistics and risk management.
first_30_days: Sign 3 niche-hobby creators with 100-300k audiences. Use their email or Patreon ZIP-code data to pick one city each. Recruit hosts from their Discords. Run the first brewery meetups and charge $12 a month from day one, aiming for 30 members per chapter.

title: Zero-Commission Motor Third-Party Renewal Rails
one_liner: If motor third-party pays agents 0%, nobody sells the mandatory cover, so insurers need a cost-plus renewal utility.
customer: Indian general insurers, especially public-sector ones, and fleet owners; insurers pay a per-renewal fee.
problem: The IRDAI draft (Sep 23) cuts commission caps from 30% to 20%, sets 0% on motor third-party and 5% on own-damage. PB Fintech fell 36% in a day, and agents and aggregators lose any reason to chase mandatory renewals.
solution: Automated renewal reminders using expiry data from dealers and registration records, sent as WhatsApp messages in local languages with UPI payment. Charge a flat servicing fee. The wedge is two-wheeler third-party renewals in one state for one insurer.
why_now: The draft is out for comment now, and insurers must find distribution that costs less than commission.
revenue_model: Rs 30-80 per renewal from the insurer, with own-damage upsell.
non_obvious_insight: When distribution stops paying, a mandatory product needs a utility rather than a marketplace, and the underwriter is the natural buyer. The draft could change, so build for both outcomes.
first_30_days: Pitch three insurers. Run a 5,000-vehicle renewal test using expiry lists from a dealer network.

title: NOI Haircut Reports for Multifamily Underwriting
one_liner: A 24-hour diligence report that restates a multifamily property's NOI for real concessions, renewal cliffs and banned fee income, sold to the lenders and buyers who will feel it first.
customer: Debt funds, CRE CLO managers, agency-lender underwriting teams and mid-market syndicators buying 100-1,000 unit properties in concession-heavy or fee-regulated markets.
problem: Headline NOI rests on face rents and other income. Concessions run 15.8% of stabilized units and 1.2M units are still in lease-up, and leases signed with free months renew at face rent a year later, inviting churn. Fee income (admin, pet, package, parking) is being banned: Seattle from July 2027 with treble damages, and the NAA tracked 140 fee bills in 2025. Sellers' T-12s show neither risk.
solution: Upload rent roll, T-12 and fee schedule and receive net-effective rent by lease cohort, concession burn-off and renewal-cliff dates, fee income at risk by jurisdiction and effective date, and a stressed NOI and DSCR. A monitoring API flags changes across a loan book as laws pass.
why_now: Concessions are now the pricing lever because rent cuts hurt valuations and algorithmic pricing is legally constrained. Dated fee bans give lenders a hard clock, and the rental supply wave has crested, so underwriting errors will show up in 2027 renewals.
revenue_model: $750-2,500 per report; $2-5K per monitored loan per year; enterprise API licenses to lenders.
non_obvious_insight: NOI has become a policy variable, but underwriting models still treat it as a market variable. The party whose model breaks first is the lender, not the operator, and lenders have diligence budgets.
first_30_days: Build a law and effective-date database for the 10 states and cities with fee rules. Publish three public teardown case studies on listed properties. Sell $500 pilot reports to 10 syndicators via LinkedIn and BiggerPockets, then pitch two debt funds on a diligence add-on.
